title: Signing key set — /jwks.json and /sandbox/jwks.json
description:
The public keys every Purpose Source signature is checked against: an RFC 7517 key set, with two members of our own on each key, `psn:status` and `psn:validityWindow` (FS08-102). Production's set is published at `/jwks.json` and the integrator test mode's at `/sandbox/jwks.json`, two disjoint documents that no route merges (FS08-103, FS10-050). The two routes answer with the `Jwks` component of `openapi/edge-public.v1.yaml`; this file is that component as one self-contained download, and `check:jwks` holds the two equal keyword for keyword, so a verifier that fetches only this file holds a key set to the same contract the routes publish.

RETIRED KEYS NEVER LEAVE (CERT-022). A rotation appends a key and re-statuses the old one; it never removes one, so a certificate signed years ago still resolves its `kid` here. A compromised key stays too: its window is the public statement of what it signed that is still accepted.

A PRODUCTION KEY STATES ITS STANDING. Every `psn-prod-` key carries `psn:status` and `psn:validityWindow`, because every public verifier refuses a production key that does not say whether, and from when to when, it was entitled to sign. A key states both members or neither, and only a test key (`psn-dev-`, `psn-sandbox-`) may state neither: a sample plane publishes its committed fixture keys that way, the verifiers accept them on their `kid` alone, and nothing they sign is a credential.

THE WINDOW. `notBefore` is inclusive and `notAfter` exclusive, so at a rotation instant exactly one key is valid. `notAfter` is null, or absent, while a key is current. A `retired` or `compromised` key states it, because the verifiers refuse a retired key whose window never closed and a compromised key that does not say where acceptance ends. JSON Schema cannot compare two instants, so a window that closes before it opens is admitted here and refused by every verifier (`key_window_malformed`): it is the shape in which the platform publishes a key WITHDRAWN when the standing its row states is one no verifier could accept.

A COMPROMISED KEY'S WINDOW ENDS WHERE ACCEPTANCE ENDS (FS08-104, CERT-023, and FS-08 §11's dated note of 2026-09-26). The set has no member of its own for a compromise instant, so on a `compromised` key `notAfter` is the instant from which nothing the key signed is accepted: the earlier of its retirement and the earliest moment someone else may have held it. It is never moved later: a key retired at R and found compromised afterwards keeps R, or forgeries dated between the two would turn from refused into accepted with a warning. A token the key signed before `notAfter` is accepted with a warning, because that date is the signer's own claim and whoever holds a compromised key can backdate it; the incident list (`key-incidents.v1`, at `/ct/incident-{date}.json`) names the transparency-log entries found forged.

HOW A VERIFIER JUDGES A SIGNATURE against the set is described in `getJwks` of the API description, and `x-psn.keyVerdict` below publishes its codes, the class of each, and the claim each protected-header `typ` is dated by.

x-psn.phase: P-M2 (`/jwks.json`: the production set committed to the website and served by the edge; from P-M3 rendered by `jobs.index-build` from `signing_keys`) · P-M4 (`/sandbox/jwks.json`, with the sandbox tenant)
x-psn.producer: P-M3: `jobs.index-build` renders the set from `signing_keys`, each key's two `psn:` members from the row's columns; the edge serves the committed production set when storage holds none
consumers: the operator's delivery and checkpoint tools

keyVerdict.rule: The published verifiers' rule, in the order `getJwks` gives it; the first step that fails decides, and each answer carries one of these codes.

outcomes.accept: the key could have made the signature then (the signature must still verify)
outcomes.warn: accepted, with something the reader must be told: the key is compromised, and the token's date is the signer's own claim
outcomes.token: refused: the TOKEN is not one this key could validly have made
outcomes.key-set: refused: the published key set does not settle the question; nothing is asserted about the token either way
outcomes.unsupported: refused: the token's `typ` is not one whose signing instant a contract fixes, so no window can be applied; nothing is asserted either way

fsRefs: FS-08 §11 (FS08-100…FS08-104) and its dated note of 2026-09-26

schemaVersion.description: The contract version, as FS-00 §6.2 asks of every artifact. Optional here because the edge mints the production set from its own bundle when storage holds none; the publishing build always stamps it.

generatedAt.description: When the publishing build produced this key set. On the published artifact it is also the response's `Last-Modified`; a minted answer carries no `Last-Modified`, and omits this member entirely when the deployment has no build instant to state — never a guessed one.

source.description: Which plane produced this artifact. `sample` and `fixture` declare a NON-PRODUCTION plane: every page that renders such an artifact is labelled sample, and a production deployment refuses to serve it (FS-10 §2 v0 note; the edge route answers `sandbox_artifact_on_prod`). `registry-v0` is the P-M2 production source of record — the curated registry repository the index is built from. `platform` is the P-M3 producer of record — the platform database, rendered by `jobs.index-build`. Optional, and its absence asserts nothing: an artifact whose body cannot carry the label borrows the plane's declaration from `/registry/index/meta.json`.

sandbox.description: `true` on `/sandbox/jwks.json` and nowhere else — the in-band marker FS08-103 asks for, so a client holding only the body still knows the set is test-mode material. ABSENT rather than `false` on the production set: which document it is decides that, and a flag saying so could be copied onto a set that is not this one.

psn:status.description: `active`: the one production key new issuance uses (FS08-101). `retired`: a rotation closed it, and what it signed inside its window keeps verifying (CERT-022). `compromised`: someone else may have held it (CERT-023); its `notAfter` says from when nothing it signed is accepted.

psn:validityWindow.description: When the key was entitled to sign: from `notBefore`, inclusive, to `notAfter`, exclusive, so at a rotation instant exactly one key is valid.

notAfter.description: The first instant the key may NOT have signed at; null, or absent, while the key is current. On a `compromised` key it is where acceptance ends: the earlier of its retirement and the earliest moment someone else may have held it, never moved later.
